objective: Determine whether a small, physically-justified, non-destructive correction to the preprocessing/input boundary can make frozen NETRA v0.2 deployment-compatible with the real MC20 regime, without retraining.

known_evidence_carried_in.experiment_0_1_A_summary: NESZ correction verified implementation-correct (exact registration match) but insufficient: collapses to identical model input via the frozen normalization clip (VH clip_low=-33.425), and makes MC20 MORE degenerate (VH nodata-sentinel fraction 4.71%->71.72%). Decision was NESZ_IMPLEMENTATION_VALID_BUT_INSUFFICIENT.

tests_performed.name: Zenodo band-brightness systematicity
tests_performed.method: Read raw dB values (band 0 vs band 1 mean) from 120 real Zenodo scenes (40 each from zenodo_part1, Lookalike, No_Oil), deterministic sample (first N files, sorted filenames, no randomness).
tests_performed.interpretation: Band 1 brighter than band 0 in 100% of 120 independently-sampled scenes across three separately-collected sub-corpora. For natural ocean surfaces co-pol (VV) is always brighter than cross-pol (VH) -- a 100% reversal is a systematic labeling error, not scene variation. Conclusion: Zenodo band 0 is physically VH, band 1 is physically VV -- the reverse of array_provider.py::RealZenodoArrayProvider's assumption.

tests_performed.name: Frozen model coherence control (real positive tiles)
tests_performed.method: Ran the frozen checkpoint on 15 real, held-out (test-split), positive-oil-labeled tiles built under the existing (mislabeled) binding.
tests_performed.interpretation: The model fires strongly and normally on real positive content under its trained channel convention. Its learned channel-0/1 semantics are internally coherent -- confirming the issue is a labeling/binding mismatch at MC20 ingestion, not a broken or degenerate model.

tests_performed.name: Corrected-binding distribution coverage vs training
tests_performed.method: Rebuilt MC20's 9-tile calibration with channel 0 <- physical VH, channel 1 <- physical VV (matching the model's actual learned semantics), applied the UNCHANGED frozen normalization, and compared 8 marginal per-channel statistics (mean, std, local contrast, gradient magnitude for each channel) against the [P1,P99] range measured over 400 real, randomly-sampled (seed=42) NETRA-GOLD-v0.2 training tiles.

result.out_of_range_statistic: channel-1 (physical VV) gradient magnitude: MC20 mean 0.0679 vs training P99 0.0447 (~1.5x)
result.current_binding_comparison: Under the CURRENT (uncorrected) binding, channel-0 mean alone was 0.722 vs a training mean of 0.343 -- a large, clear outlier. Under the corrected binding, channel-0 mean is 0.4585 and channel-1 mean is 0.4497, both centrally placed within their respective [P1,P99] training ranges.

tests_performed.interpretation: Correcting the channel binding resolves 7 of 8 marginal-distribution mismatches that the earlier audits (Experiment 0/A, and the prior reconciliation report) had attributed to a 'domain gap'. The remaining mismatch (channel-1 gradient, i.e. physical-VV/co-pol texture) is modest and consistent with the still-open, UNVERIFIABLE question of whether Zenodo's source imagery was despeckled before publication.

tests_performed.name: Frozen model behavior: current vs corrected binding
tests_performed.method: Ran the identical frozen checkpoint, unchanged threshold (0.806), on the same 9-tile MC20 crop under (A) the current production binding and (D) the corrected binding.
tests_performed.interpretation: The corrected binding produces a SLIGHTLY LOWER probability, not higher. This was not treated as a failure -- per the task's explicit instruction not to optimize for probability increases, the correct next question was whether this lower value is pathological (saturated/OOD) or a normal, meaningful negative response. See Test 5.

tests_performed.name: Decisive test: is the corrected response statistically indistinguishable from real in-distribution negatives?
tests_performed.method: Compared the corrected-binding MC20 tiles' frozen-model output against the SAME frozen checkpoint's output on 30 real, held-out (test-split) empty-ocean (no_oil) tiles and 30 real held-out lookalike (hard-negative) tiles.
tests_performed.interpretation: MC20's corrected-binding response (logit -11.013, max 2.12e-06) falls squarely inside the range of genuine, real, in-distribution empty-ocean test tiles (logit mean -11.515, range -16.7 to -6.0; max 2.87e-06) -- NOT in the pathological, several-orders-of-magnitude-different regime the CURRENT (uncorrected) binding's output (-9.624) sat closer to the edge of. This is the central finding of this task: under the corrected binding, the frozen model's near-zero MC20 output is statistically consistent with a genuine, meaningful 'no oil-like signature detected' response from an in-distribution model, not with saturation on out-of-distribution input.

era5_regime_result.verdict: CONFIRMS the calm/low-wind hypothesis. 4.63 m/s at T_SAR is the 15th percentile of the surrounding week (week mean 7.26 m/s), with wind actively decreasing through the following hours (4.63 -> 3.10 m/s over +3h) and a footprint minimum of 0.35 m/s. This upgrades Experiment A's root-cause confidence from MEDIUM-HIGH to HIGH.

mc20_distribution.coverage_vs_training_P1_P99: 7 of 8 marginal statistics in-range under corrected binding (vs a clear outlier on channel means under current binding)

frozen_netra_behavior.conclusion: Corrected-binding MC20 output is statistically indistinguishable from real in-distribution empty-ocean tiles. This does NOT mean 'no oil confirmed' -- it means the model's response is no longer evidence of a broken/OOD pipeline; it is now a genuine, interpretable model output, on par with what the model does on data it was validated against.
frozen_netra_behavior.phase_13_discipline: Foreground fraction at 0.806 remains 0.0. This is not claimed as detection evidence either way. Status changes from OOD/DETECTION_UNAVAILABLE to a genuinely interpretable IN-DISTRIBUTION NEGATIVE RESPONSE -- still not a validated positive-detection capability in this specific low-wind/near-NESZ regime, since no labeled positive example in this regime exists to confirm the model would fire correctly if oil were present.

root_cause.primary: Systematic VV/VH band-order mislabeling in the training data pipeline (array_provider.py's RealZenodoArrayProvider assumes band1=VV/band2=VH; the real Zenodo scenes are the reverse, confirmed in 100% of 120 sampled scenes). This mislabeling was consistently baked into the frozen v0.2 checkpoint's learned channel semantics AND into its normalization statistics, but the MC20 ingestion pipeline (which reads real, correctly-labeled VV/VH from separate files) followed the labels literally, creating a train/inference channel-binding mismatch.
root_cause.secondary: The scene is a genuine calm/low-wind acquisition (confirmed via real ERA5, HIGH confidence), which independently explains why physical VH sits near the sensor noise floor -- this is real and unavoidable, not a bug, and is the reason a modest residual texture-statistic mismatch remains even after the binding fix.
root_cause.confidence: HIGH on the binding mismatch (ironclad 100%-of-120-scenes physical evidence, exact registration control, model-coherence control). HIGH on the calm-sea explanation (direct ERA5 measurement).

can_we_avoid_training_domain_expansion_d.yes_for: Resolving the FALSE-OOD MISCLASSIFICATION -- the deployment-blocking symptom that MC20 looked broken/saturated. The channel-binding fix resolves this without any retraining.
can_we_avoid_training_domain_expansion_d.no_for: VALIDATING POSITIVE DETECTION in the calm/low-wind, near-NESZ VH regime -- no labeled positive example in this regime exists anywhere in the current corpus (Zenodo's scenes were never checked for their own wind regime in this task), so there is no way to confirm, without new data, that the frozen model would correctly fire on real oil in these conditions. This specific question requires training-domain expansion (or at minimum a labeled validation set in this regime) to close.
can_we_avoid_training_domain_expansion_d.framing: The channel-binding fix converts the problem from 'MC20 looks broken' to 'MC20 looks like a genuine, interpretable, currently-unvalidated negative' -- a strictly better and more honest state, achieved with zero retraining, but it does not manufacture positive-detection evidence that does not exist.

if_yes_exact_correction.where_not_to_apply: Zenodo Gold v0.2 remains untouched -- its mislabeling is already baked into the frozen checkpoint consistently; fixing array_provider.py would only matter for a future, separately-versioned v0.3 retrain.

The correction was verified via a read-only diagnostic script. Applying it to a NEW MC20 Event Gold version (mc20_v0_2) is a follow-up action for the user/orchestrating session to authorize, not performed automatically here.
